heart_rate.medical: Resting pulse. TB causes sympathetic activation -> mild tachycardia.

spo2.medical: Oxygen saturation. Pulmonary TB damages alveoli -> subtle desaturation.

resp_rate.medical: Breathing rate. Compensatory increase when gas exchange is impaired.

temperature.medical: Core body temp. TB hallmark: low-grade evening fever (37.2-38.0°C).

wbc_count.medical: White blood cells. Mild leukocytosis in active TB.

esr.medical: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate. Non-specific inflammation marker. Elevated 40-100+ in active TB.

crp.medical: C-Reactive Protein. Acute phase reactant. Rises sharply in active infection.

lymphocyte_pct.medical: Lymphocyte percentage of WBC. TB causes lymphocyte-predominant response, especially in pleural fluid.

hemoglobin.medical: Oxygen-carrying protein. Chronic TB causes anemia of chronic disease (normocytic normochromic).

albumin.medical: Serum albumin. Drops in chronic TB due to malnutrition, liver stress, and protein wasting.

xray_opacity.medical: Overall lung opacity/haziness. Infiltrates, consolidation, fibrosis. Upper lobe predominance in reactivation TB.

xray_cavity.medical: Cavitation presence. Hallmark of active pulmonary TB. Indicates high bacterial load and infectiousness.

xray_nodule.medical: Micronodular pattern. Miliary TB: random 1-3mm nodules throughout both lungs. Hematogenous spread.

xray_pleural.medical: Pleural effusion/thickening. Common in primary TB and TB pleurisy. Often unilateral.

ada_level.medical: Adenosine Deaminase. THE gold standard biomarker for TB pleural effusion. >40 U/L highly suggestive of TB.

mantoux_mm.medical: Tuberculin Skin Test (TST) induration. >10mm in immunocompetent = positive. >5mm in HIV+ = positive.
